B1:
Touched fires many times (several body parts, repeated contacts) before Destroy takes effect, and each queued handler awards coins (with deferred signals they all run). Fix with a debounce flag set before awarding:
```lua
local part = script.Parent
local taken = false
part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
  if taken then return end
  local plr = game.Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
  if not plr then return end
  local hum = hit.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
  taken = true
  plr.leaderstats.Coins.Value += 10
  part:Destroy()
end)
```
Run it in a server Script, not on the client.
B2: With StreamingEnabled the client only has instances near the player; far doors (or their parent models) aren't streamed in at script start, so direct indexing errors. Fix 1: wait for it with timeouts: workspace:WaitForChild("Map"):WaitForChild("Buildings"):WaitForChild("Hotel"):WaitForChild("Door", 30), handle nil, and set the Hotel/Door model's ModelStreamingMode = Atomic so it arrives whole. Fix 2 (preferred for many doors): tag doors with CollectionService and use GetTagged + GetInstanceAddedSignal("Door") / GetInstanceRemovedSignal to connect and disconnect as they stream in/out. (Or detect the touch on the server, which always has the whole map; Persistent mode only as a last resort.)
B3: Bugs: (1) plr can be nil (player left) - plr.UserId errors inside the pcall and is ignored. (2) The pcall result is ignored: PurchaseGranted is returned even when the save failed -> charged, nothing. (3) No PurchaseId idempotency: Roblox retries receipts, so a retry after a save that actually succeeded grants twice. (4) GetAsync+SetAsync is not atomic - races with other servers/saves lose or duplicate coins; and writing a separate store from live session data lets the session save overwrite it. (5) Only one ProcessReceipt may exist. Correct: if the player isn't present / data not loaded return NotProcessedYet; in one UpdateAsync on the player's document, if receipts[PurchaseId] exists return unchanged, else add 100 coins and record the PurchaseId together; return PurchaseGranted only if that write succeeded, otherwise NotProcessedYet; then update in-memory coins/UI.
B4: Remote arguments are serialized: tables are copied as plain data and metatables (and functions) are stripped, so the client gets {Name='Rifle', Ammo=30} without Weapon's methods -> w:Fire is nil. Instances are sent as references, but ServerStorage contents never replicate to clients, so the reference arrives as nil. Fix: send plain data (or an id) and rebuild on the client with a shared ModuleScript in ReplicatedStorage (`setmetatable(data, Weapon)` / `Weapon.new(data)`). For the part, keep it in ReplicatedStorage (or clone it into Workspace/a replicated container before firing), or send its name and let the client look it up in ReplicatedStorage.
B5:
workspace:Raycast's direction is the full ray vector - its length is the ray distance. A .Unit vector is 1 stud long, so the ray stops after 1 stud. Fix: use the displacement or unit * range, and exclude the shooter:
```lua
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {shooterCharacter}
local dir = (target - origin).Unit * 500  -- or (target - origin)
local r = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
if r then print(r.Instance, r.Position) end
```
B6: When the last player leaves, the server begins shutting down and doesn't wait for the yielding SetAsync in PlayerRemoving, so the save is killed or never completes. Fix: game:BindToClose that saves every remaining player in parallel (task.spawn each) and waits until all finish or a ~25 s deadline (the window is 30 s), also waiting for in-flight PlayerRemoving saves; make saves idempotent per player (saving/saved flag) so PlayerRemoving and BindToClose don't double-write; use UpdateAsync with retries plus periodic autosave so little is lost. In Studio, keep it short (RunService:IsStudio()).

B8:
```lua
local MPS = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local store = game:GetService("DataStoreService"):GetDataStore("PlayerData")
local PRODUCTS = { [123456] = function(d) d.Gems = (d.Gems or 0) + 100 end } -- Gems100

MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info) -- the ONLY assignment in the game
  local grant = PRODUCTS[info.ProductId]
  if not grant then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
  if not player or not Session.isLoaded(player) then
    return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet -- retried when they rejoin
  end
  local ok, err = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, "u_" .. info.PlayerId, function(d)
    d = d or {}
    if not Session.ownsLock(d) then return nil end
    d.Receipts = d.Receipts or {}
    if d.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] then return d end -- already granted
    grant(d)
    d.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] = os.time() -- prune old ids over time
    return d
  end)
  if not ok then warn(err) return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  Session.refresh(player) -- sync in-memory Gems/UI from the saved doc
  return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end
```
Grant and PurchaseId are written atomically in the same document; never grant in PromptProductPurchaseFinished.

```lua
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local info = TweenInfo.new(0.4, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
local OPEN = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0)
local CLOSED = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1.5, 0)

  current:Play()
end

local function close()
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  local t = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = CLOSED})
  current = t
  t.Completed:Connect(function(state)
    if state == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed and current == t then
      menu.Visible = false
    end
  end)
  t:Play()
end
```

```lua
local MAX_RANGE, DAMAGE = 200, 20
local function shoot(player: Player, targetPos: Vector3)
  if typeof(targetPos) ~= "Vector3" or targetPos ~= targetPos then return end
  local char = player.Character
  local head = char and char:FindFirstChild("Head")
  local myHum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if not head or not myHum or myHum.Health <= 0 then return end
  local origin = head.Position
  local offset = targetPos - origin

  params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {char}

  if not result then return end
  local model = result.Instance:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
  local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if hum and hum.Health > 0 then
    hum:TakeDamage(DAMAGE)
  end
  return result
end
```

```lua
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local TAG = "KillBrick"
local conns: {[Instance]: RBXScriptConnection} = {}

local function onAdded(part)
  if not part:IsA("BasePart") or conns[part] then return end
  conns[part] = part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)

  end)

local function onRemoved(part)
  local c = conns[part]
  if c then c:Disconnect(); conns[part] = nil end
end

CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(TAG):Connect(onAdded)
CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(TAG):Connect(onRemoved)
```

Removed fires on tag removal and when the part is destroyed, so the table doesn't leak.

```lua
local TeleportService = game:GetService("TeleportService")
local MAX_TRIES, BACKOFF = 4, 2

local function safeTeleport(placeId: number, players: {Player}, teleportData: any?)
  local options = Instance.new("TeleportOptions")
  if teleportData then options:SetTeleportData(teleportData) end
  local ok, result
  for attempt = 1, MAX_TRIES do
    ok, result = pcall(TeleportService.TeleportAsync, TeleportService, placeId, players, options)
    if ok then return true, result end
    warn("Teleport failed:", result)
    task.wait(BACKOFF * attempt)
  end
  return false, result
end

local retries: {[Player]: number} = {}
TeleportService.TeleportInitFailed:Connect(function(player, result, msg, placeId, options)
  if result == Enum.TeleportResult.IsTeleporting then return end
  local n = (retries[player] or 0) + 1
  retries[player] = n
  if n > MAX_TRIES or result == Enum.TeleportResult.Unauthorized then return end
  task.wait(BACKOFF * n)
  if player.Parent then
    pcall(TeleportService.TeleportAsync, TeleportService, placeId, {player}, options)
  end
end)
game.Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) retries[p] = nil end)
```
Save/release player data before teleporting; teleport data passes through the client, so don't trust it.
B13: Buy (client -> server): a RemoteEvent (e.g. BuyItem) carrying only intent (itemId), or a client->server RemoteFunction if the UI needs a success/failure reply. The server owns the coin balance and price table and validates (types, item exists, enough coins, rate limit), then deducts and grants. Counter update (server -> client): a RemoteEvent FireClient with the new balance, or replicate the value (leaderstats IntValue / player attribute) and have the UI listen to Changed/GetAttributeChangedSignal. Don't use RemoteFunction:InvokeClient: the server thread yields on the client, which can never return (hang), error, or return garbage, and errors if the client leaves - an exploiter can stall server code. The client's display is cosmetic only.
B14: Teleport data (TeleportOptions:SetTeleportData / GetJoinData().TeleportData) goes through the client, so it's visible and spoofable, size-limited, and lost if the teleport fails or the player rejoins directly - fine only for non-authoritative hints (party/match id, map, preferred loadout to be validated). Coin balance must stay authoritative: keep it in the player's session-locked DataStore record (save and release before teleport, load in the match place). MemoryStore (hash/sorted map with TTL) suits fast, short-lived cross-server state like match assignment or the chosen loadout, but isn't durable. Choice: DataStore for coins and owned items; loadout in the DataStore profile or a MemoryStore entry keyed by userId, validated server-side against ownership; teleport data only for non-sensitive routing info.
B15: Per-instance Scripts: 610 copies of near-identical code, each with its own thread and connections; hard to update (edit every copy, drift), more memory and startup cost, and awkward with spawning/streaming. Tag-driven: tag instances (Door, Pickup, Turret) with CollectionService; one server Script/module per tag uses GetTagged + GetInstanceAddedSignal to bind behaviour and GetInstanceRemovedSignal to clean up (per-instance state/connections in a table keyed by instance, disconnected on removal); per-instance config via Attributes. Newly spawned instances bind automatically when a tagged template is cloned; on clients with StreamingEnabled, streamed-in instances fire InstanceAdded and streamed-out fire InstanceRemoved, so client visuals bind/unbind correctly. Turrets can share one Heartbeat loop over the tracked set instead of one loop each.
B16: Give the driver network ownership of the car assembly (when the VehicleSeat occupant changes, SetNetworkOwner(player) on the chassis; back to server (nil) when they exit), since server-owned physics feels laggy for the driver. Risk: the owning client fully controls that assembly's physics - exploiters can teleport, speed-hack, fly, fling other players or skip checkpoints. The server must still validate: speed/position deltas over time (caps, teleport detection), checkpoint order and lap times (server-side triggers/distance checks), race results and rewards, effects on other players, and that only the actually seated driver gets ownership; set unoccupied cars to server ownership (disable auto ownership) and never trust client-reported results.
B17: Use an UnreliableRemoteEvent for aim/position updates: unordered, may drop, no retransmit - fine for state superseded by the next update. Constraints: payload limit ~1000 bytes (larger is dropped), no ordering guarantee, per-client throttle (excess dropped, not queued), dropped if no handler is connected. Handling: send only on change, throttled to ~10-20 Hz; keep payloads small (pitch/yaw numbers or packed buffer rather than CFrames); include a sequence number/timestamp and ignore stale packets; interpolate on receivers; keep important events (fire, hit claims, reload) on reliable RemoteEvents; validate and rate-limit on the server. Position already replicates via character physics, so don't send it.
B18: Put NPCs under many Actors (one per NPC or per group), each with a Script that runs the heavy work in parallel: RunService.Heartbeat:ConnectParallel (or task.desynchronize) to do raycasts (workspace:Raycast is parallel-safe) and path scoring, keep results in locals, then task.synchronize() before writing Instance properties (movement, damage, attributes). Limitations: no Instance writes or most mutating APIs in the parallel phase (reads only); each Actor has its own Lua VM, so module state isn't shared - use SharedTable (atomic ops like SharedTable.increment) or Actor messaging (SendMessage / BindToMessageParallel); scripts must be descendants of the Actor; sync/desync switches cost time, so batch work; some APIs (e.g. PathfindingService ComputeAsync) aren't parallel-safe; also stagger work across frames instead of every NPC every Heartbeat. Profile with the MicroProfiler.
B19: Turn on Workspace.StreamingEnabled (set in Studio; not scriptable). Sensible values: StreamingMinRadius 64 (default), StreamingTargetRadius default 1024, lower (e.g. 256-512) for mobile-heavy open worlds; StreamOutBehavior Opportunistic; StreamingIntegrityMode PauseOutsideLoadedArea. Set ModelStreamingMode = Atomic on interactive models so they arrive whole, Persistent only rarely (PersistentPerPlayer for a player's own base), and Model LevelOfDetail = StreamingMesh for distant landmarks. Scripts: client code must not assume parts exist - WaitForChild with timeouts (on Atomic models), CollectionService tags with InstanceAdded/Removed for streamed parts, handle stream-out (instances disappear), call Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync before moving/teleporting players server-side, and keep authoritative logic on the server (it has the whole map).
B20: Each SetAsync is a write request. 80 players every 5 s = ~960 writes/min from one server, far above the per-server write budget (~60 + 40 x players per minute, with the experience-wide 300 + 20 x CCU cap) and the per-key ~6 s write cooldown, so requests queue; when the queue (30) is full further calls fail immediately (301-306 throttle errors, 302 queue full) -> lost saves. Better: keep data cached in memory, mark dirty on change, autosave each player every 2-3 minutes with staggered timers/jitter and only if dirty; save on PlayerRemoving, before teleports, after important purchases, and in BindToClose; use UpdateAsync with session locking and exponential-backoff retries; check DataStoreService:GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before non-critical writes; or use ProfileStore.
B21: In Studio: open the Assistant panel, click its ... menu > Manage MCP Servers, and turn on 'Enable Studio as MCP server', then add Studio's MCP server in the external client's config. Tools it exposes include list_roblox_studios, get_studio_state, search_game_tree, inspect_instance, script_read, script_search, script_grep, multi_edit, execute_luau, start_stop_play, get_console_output, screen_capture, character_navigation, user_keyboard_input, user_mouse_input, search_asset, insert_asset, upload_image, generate_mesh, generate_material, generate_procedural_model, wait_job_finished, http_get, subagent and skill.
B22: Core instances: InputContext (a group of actions; Enabled, Priority, Sink), InputAction (a named action with a Type such as Bool, Direction1D/2D; fires Pressed, Released and StateChanged, readable via GetState()), and InputBinding (child of an action mapping a KeyCode, gamepad input or a touch UIButton to it). A Bool action signals a press by firing Pressed (Released on let-go; StateChanged(true/false)). For a menu: create a Menu InputContext with a higher Priority than the default player-script/gameplay context and Sink = true, and enable it when the menu opens; inputs bound in it are consumed and don't reach lower-priority contexts (movement, jump). Disable it (and re-enable gameplay) when the menu closes.
B23: Roblox UI Styling (Style Editor, beta) applies CSS-like rules to GuiObjects. Instances: StyleSheet (container of rules), StyleRule (a Selector - class name like TextButton, tag/class ".Primary", "#Name", pseudo-states/children - plus properties set via SetProperty/SetProperties), StyleDerive (makes a sheet inherit another, e.g. a token/theme sheet), StyleLink (put under a ScreenGui/UI tree; its StyleSheet property links a sheet so its rules apply to that tree), and StyleQuery for responsive/conditional rules. Styles reach UI by linking via StyleLink and matching selectors against instances (CollectionService tags act as classes). Tokens: define attributes on a token StyleSheet (e.g. PrimaryColor) and reference them in rule properties as "$PrimaryColor"; swapping the derived token sheet re-themes every rule using it.
B24: Method: Facial Age Estimation through the device camera in the Roblox app (vendor-processed, images deleted afterwards), with ID verification as an option for 13+. Age groups: under 9, 9-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-20, 21+. Restriction: after checking, users can chat only with their own group and adjacent groups (e.g. 9-12 with under-9 and 13-15); under-16s can't chat with adults; without a check, chat is unavailable (Trusted Connections can be exceptions). Rolled out in some regions late 2025, globally from January 2026. Games shouldn't make gameplay depend on chat.
